newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers deal seen signed by Wed - Treu.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers deal seen signed by Wed - Treu.

text.p: Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said he expected a settlement ending a months-long pay dispute in Italy's engineering and metalworking industry to be signed later on Tuesday or on Wednesday, Italian television reported.
The three unions in the sector, FIM, FIOM and UILM, said earlier that they had endorsed a government proposal to end the dispute, based on a 30-month contract.
Employers' groups Intersind, representing state industries, and Confapi, grouping small and medium-sized businesses, also said they had approved the proposal.
The biggest employers' group, Federmeccanica, was expected to give its response at a meeting at the Labour Ministry on Tuesday evening (after 1800 GMT).
"It seems to me that people are broadly in favour" of the proposal, television quoted Treu as saying.

"I want to check it out this evening and if there is a positive response we will move to signing immediately. If it's not this evening it will be tomorrow morning," Treu said. --Rome newsroom +39 6 678 2505
